tasks.title: Corrupt subscriber stores exit 2 with one escaped diagnostic and released locks
tasks.spec: ## Repository: notify, Behavior, Tests regressions 1-12 and controls 13-15 plus existing-suite controls, Docs, and Checks and completion evidence 1-13; Required behavior 1-6 (including 4a-4f); Performance impact; Security impact; Counterexamples. One change implements the CLI fix, its regression tests and both docs; fix and tests land in the same commit because of per-file coverage. Use the exact N/S/T/R fixture recipes and independent literal path expectations in the current plan. Preserve the store call sequence and base-relative store/sidecar state; byte equality and no-sidecar evidence is limited to the proven fixtures. Keep store format, protected store implementation, service startup, unsupported commands and other exit codes unchanged. Record actual pre-edit BASE; if both required valid executable delete invocations on N already return 2 there, request a hold instead of review. Evidence files, coverage config and harnesses stay outside the implementation checkout and are created/edited with file tools.

printf '%s\n' "$BASE"
bun --version
bun install --frozen-lockfile
acceptance.expected: Record the actual pre-edit implementation BASE in the PR body and retain it for all comparisons; the planning snapshot is not a substitute. Bun prints 1.4.0; frozen installation exits 0, with hooks enabled and no tracked dependency or configuration change. Never bypass hooks or weaken lint, typecheck or coverage.

Both commands exit 0. Copy only the new test/subscribers-cli.corrupt-store.test.ts into this disposable BASE worktree using file tools. With file tools create /tmp/notify-nocov/bunfig.toml containing only [test] and coverage = false. Keep both tracked bunfig.toml files unchanged. Use the spec's exact N/S/T/R fixture recipes and only imports present on BASE, node:assert/strict, per-test tempDir cleanup, printable ASCII test names and escaped non-ASCII source characters. If both required executable invocations on N already return 2 on BASE, request a hold instead of opening a review.

acceptance.command: for run in 1 2 3; do (cd /tmp/notify-base && bun --config=/tmp/notify-nocov/bunfig.toml test test/subscribers-cli.corrupt-store.test.ts); done
acceptance.expected: Each of three separate isolated runs exits 1 and reports exactly 12 fail, 3 pass, corresponding to Repository: notify Tests 1-12 and controls 13-15. Executable N with probe@example.com and Absent@Example.com fails status 1 !== 2 and prints SQLiteError: file is not a database; public N and all five path cases throw SQLITE_NOTADB; S with each address throws SQLITE_CORRUPT during open; T and R with stored probe@example.com throw SQLITE_CORRUPT in deleteByEmail. Record names and reasons for every run. All three controls pass on BASE. Missing imports, setup errors and coverage failures are not acceptable red evidence.

acceptance.command: for run in 1 2 3; do bun --config=/tmp/notify-nocov/bunfig.toml test test/subscribers-cli.corrupt-store.test.ts || exit "$?"; done
acceptance.expected: All three branch runs exit 0 with exactly 15 pass, 0 fail, covering Repository: notify Tests 1-15. Tests 1-2 spawn process.execPath with src/index.ts subscribers delete probe@example.com and, on a fresh N, Absent@Example.com; environment is only PATH and PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE. Each exits 2, stdout is empty, stderr equals pulse-notify: cannot use subscription store <file>: the file is corrupt or not a database followed by one newline. Tests 3-6 return exactly { lines: [that diagnostic without its final newline], code: 2 } for public N, S with each address and T with stored probe@example.com. Do not require T with an absent address to fail. Apply shared assertions C from the spec to cases 1-11: full byte equality, absent lock, directory listing exactly the fixture filename, immediate acquireLock(..., testLockDeps()).release(), and absence of argument/normalized addresses, sentinel, SQLite and stack frames. Fixtures use 50 rows and the exact page damage of the plan; no global or module mocks or test-only exports. Tests 7-11 use the five input names and literal shown names from the plan's path table: LF -> \u000a, CR -> \u000d, CRLF -> \u000d\u000a, literal backslash-n -> doubled backslash plus n, and U+2028/NEL/DEL/ESC -> \u2028/\u0085/\u007f/\u001b. Build expected strings from join(dir, literal shown name), never the escaping helper under test. The escape rule doubles backslash and replaces every Cc, U+2028 and U+2029 with \u plus four lowercase hex digits; no other change, quotes or raw line separators. Use Unicode property escapes with the u flag, not control-character ranges or JSON.stringify. Test 12 on R returns the fixed diagnostic/code 2, leaves no lock, and readdirSync is exactly the fixture filename with no WAL, SHM or journal; output has no address or sentinel. Header bytes 18/19 change from [1, 1] to [2, 2], big-endian counters at offsets 24 and 92 each increase by 1, and file length is unchanged. Restoring only offsets 18, 19, 24-27 and 92-95 from before makes after equal before. Do not assert byte equality for R: this is protected SubscriberStore.open behavior on BASE too. N and damaged WAL fixtures S/T retain complete byte equality. These fixture assertions are not a universal byte or sidecar guarantee; checkpoint failures after a committed delete are code-reading-only coverage.

acceptance.command:
(cd /tmp/notify-base && bun --config=/tmp/notify-nocov/bunfig.toml test test/subscribers-cli.test.ts test/index.test.ts test/subscriptions-store.test.ts)

acceptance.expected: Both commands exit 0, 0 fail; record actual pass counts separately on BASE and branch. Existing suites preserve normalized healthy deletion (deleted 1 then deleted 0), whitespace normalization, missing-store deleted 0 without creation, held-lock code 2 with the owner's lock intact, executable usage/exit 1, service-held lock refusal and user_version=2 refusal. Also record the new file's controls 13-15 passing on both revisions: list/no args/delete without address/delete with an extra argument return usage: pulse-notify subscribers delete <address> and code 1 before touching N; invalid address returns pulse-notify: subscribers delete: invalid address/code 1; bytes unchanged and no lock. user_version=2 returns pulse-notify: PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE: the store has an unknown format/code 2 with no lock. A directory path throws SQLiteError with code SQLITE_CANTOPEN and leaves no lock. Unsupported commands retain exit 1.

acceptance.command:
bun /tmp/notify-store-fixtures.ts
for fixture in N S T R; do
  fixture_root="/tmp/notify-store-state/$fixture"
  base_status=0
  (cd /tmp/notify-base && env -i PATH="$PATH" PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE="$fixture_root/base/store.db" bun src/index.ts subscribers delete probe@example.com) || base_status=$?
  branch_status=0
  env -i PATH="$PATH" PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE="$fixture_root/branch/store.db" bun src/index.ts subscribers delete probe@example.com || branch_status=$?
  printf '%s base=%s branch=%s\n' "$fixture" "$base_status" "$branch_status"
  test "$base_status" -eq 1 && test "$branch_status" -eq 2 || exit 1
  cmp "$fixture_root/base/store.db" "$fixture_root/branch/store.db" || exit 1
  test "$(ls -A "$fixture_root/base")" = store.db && test "$(ls -A "$fixture_root/branch")" = store.db || exit 1
  ls -A "$fixture_root/base"
  ls -A "$fixture_root/branch"
  if test "$fixture" = R; then
    compare_status=0
    cmp -l "$fixture_root/original.db" "$fixture_root/branch/store.db" || compare_status=$?
    test "$compare_status" -eq 1 || exit 1
  else
    cmp "$fixture_root/original.db" "$fixture_root/branch/store.db" || exit 1
  fi
done
acceptance.expected: Create /tmp/notify-store-fixtures.ts with file tools outside the implementation checkout before running this acceptance. It builds exactly one original for each of N, S, T and R using the plan's recipes and the branch SubscriberStore, then makes byte-identical copies at /tmp/notify-store-state/<N|S|T|R>/base/store.db and branch/store.db in fresh separate directories containing only store.db. Builder exits 0. Each BASE CLI exits 1, each branch CLI exits 2 with the fixed diagnostic; retain stdout/stderr and record all statuses. For every fixture, cmp of base and branch artifacts exits 0; both directory listings are exactly store.db (no WAL, SHM, journal or lock). N, S and T also compare equal to original.db. For R only, cmp -l original.db branch/store.db exits 1: one-based offsets 19 and 20 go from 1 to 2, and only bytes 25-28 and 93-96 may also differ; both big-endian counters increase by 1, usually changing only 28 and 96 unless a carry occurs. Record actual offsets/byte values and all comparisons/listings. The shell acceptance exits 0 only when the expected statuses and comparisons hold. This independently verifies Required behavior 4b and 4e for the four proven fixtures; it does not prove unchanged bytes or absent sidecars for arbitrary checkpoint failures.

acceptance.command:
env -i PATH="$PATH" PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE=/tmp/notify-smoke-corrupt/store.db bun src/index.ts subscribers delete probe@example.com
env -i PATH="$PATH" PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE=$'/tmp/notify-smoke-newline/a\nb.db' bun src/index.ts subscribers delete probe@example.com
env -i PATH="$PATH" PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE=/tmp/notify-smoke-healthy/store.db bun src/index.ts subscribers delete probe@example.com
acceptance.expected: Prepare fresh N fixtures at the ordinary and LF paths and a healthy format-1 fixture containing probe@example.com, using file tools for scratch files. Record each real-CLI command, status, stdout and stderr. Both N commands exit 2, stdout empty, exactly one stderr line with the fixed diagnostic; the LF path prints /tmp/notify-smoke-newline/a\u000ab.db and captured stderr has wc -l = 1. Check byte preservation and lock release. The healthy command exits 0 and prints deleted 1. This exercises the changed CLI as required by notify AGENTS.md; do not start the long-running service.

acceptance.command:
(cd /tmp/notify-base && env -i PATH="$PATH" PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE=/tmp/notify-smoke-schema-base/store.db bun src/index.ts subscribers delete probe@example.com)
env -i PATH="$PATH" PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE=/tmp/notify-smoke-schema-branch/store.db bun src/index.ts subscribers delete probe@example.com
acceptance.expected: Prepare independent format-1 stores with SubscriberStore, close them, set PRAGMA user_version = 2 using raw Database connections, then close. On BASE and branch, the real-CLI control exits 2 with empty stdout and stderr exactly pulse-notify: PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE: the store has an unknown format followed by one newline. No .lock remains. Record both results; this carries the issue review's executable schema-version baseline control.

Exit 0 for full lint, typecheck and tests under normal committed coverage settings; the spec's literal branch count is 811 pass, 0 fail (796 on BASE). src/subscribers-cli.ts line coverage is at least 80 %, cognitive complexity at most 15 per function. Source fix and regression tests land together so per-file coverage stays green; include both docs in the same change. Report Bun 1.4.0. Do not substitute focused coverage runs for this gate.

Code review proves Required behavior 1-6, especially 4a-4f, and the Security impact checklist. Only instanceof SQLiteError with (errno & 0xff) in {11, 26} maps to the fixed code-2 diagnostic, including extended variants and errors at open, delete/its checkpoint or close. Keep argument/address validation before acquiring the lock or opening the store. Once acquired, lock release is guaranteed on success, handled/rethrown errors and close throws. Make exactly the same store calls as BASE in the same order: openExisting once, deleteByEmail once if a store was returned, then close once even after a delete error. Add no SQLite statement, pragma, second open, checkpoint, header pre-check, integrity scan, repair or store/sidecar file access. First error wins: if delete throws, attempt close and discard its error before classifying/rethrowing the delete error; if only close throws, classify/rethrow that error. Delete SQLITE_CORRUPT plus close SQLITE_IOERR gives code 2; delete SQLITE_BUSY plus close SQLITE_CORRUPT rethrows SQLITE_BUSY (executable exit 1). Other exceptions are rethrown. Preserve ConfigError/StartupError text, SUBSCRIBERS_USAGE, INVALID_ADDRESS_LINE and exports. Keep runSubscribers' doc comment accurate: corrupt store is exit 2, with no unconditional byte/sidecar or nothing-deleted promise. The result carries only the escaped configured path and fixed reason, never raw SQLite messages, file content, address, errno/code or stack. Review hostile file bytes, damaged rows, R, escaped paths, validation precedence, normalized/whitespace addresses and directory-path control. Store state is relative to BASE: damage found at a checkpoint after commit leaves the delete committed and can leave WAL/SHM, exactly as on BASE; exit 2 does not confirm whether the address was deleted. Byte and absent-sidecar guarantees apply only to proven N/S/T/R assertions. Explicitly report close-throw lock release, first-error-wins and SQLITE_CORRUPT_* variants as code-reading-only coverage, same-call-order evidence as code reading plus the four-fixture comparison, and raw-path lock messages as a known limit. No changes outside the four allowed files.
Exit 1 with no output: both files hold only ASCII. Every non-ASCII test character is written as a Unicode escape, and test names hold only printable ASCII.

Both documents describe the exact pulse-notify: cannot use subscription store <path>: the file is corrupt or not a database line, exit 2, escaped path, no address and released lock, matching the independent test literals. README adds one short sentence to the email-subscriptions paragraph and links docs/operation.md#subscriber-store; it leaves byte details to the operator docs. The operator deletion bullet specifies backslash as \\ and Cc/U+2028/U+2029 as \uXXXX (lowercase four-digit hex), no output line holds the address, the lock is released, and the command does not repair the file and makes the same SQLite calls as any delete, with no extra check or write. Exit 2 does not confirm whether the address was deleted: corruption found only at a checkpoint after the delete commits leaves the deletion in place and can leave WAL/SHM, as on BASE. Byte and sidecar statements must match Required behavior 4e and its proven fixtures: non-database N and damaged WAL S/T with damage found before commit stay byte for byte unchanged; externally switched rollback-journal R has its journal-mode header set back to WAL on open, as today. No unconditional unchanged-bytes/no-sidecars/nothing-deleted claim anywhere in README, docs/operation.md, runSubscribers' doc comment or the PR body. Advise restore the store from a backup, then run subscribers delete <address> again. Do not document a new command, repair or startup change. Leave the service Exit codes table unchanged. Both docs remain in the same change, matching the plan and issue review's exact file set.

acceptance.command: test -z "$(git -C /tmp/notify-base status --porcelain)" && for pair in 1 2 3 4 5; do (cd /tmp/notify-base && { TIMEFORMAT='%U %S'; time bun run test; }) || exit "$?"; (TIMEFORMAT='%U %S'; time bun run test) || exit "$?"; done
acceptance.expected: Before measuring, remove only the copied regression file from /tmp/notify-base with file tools; git status --porcelain there is empty. All ten full-suite runs exit 0 in base, branch, base, branch order, five per revision, with the same pinned dependencies, Bun 1.4.0 and normal coverage settings. Measure using the Bash time keyword, which includes waited-for child CPU; do not depend on /usr/bin/time. Report every user, sys and user+sys sample, each side's median (third-smallest of five sums), and median(branch) minus median(base), rounded to 0.01 s. The revised plan estimates +0.4 to +0.8 s; flag a delta above +1.0 s for review. Describe shared-machine noise and test CPU, without claiming wall-time or service improvements. No Docker bench (#834).

acceptance.command:
base_source_bytes=$(git cat-file -s "$BASE":src/subscribers-cli.ts) &&
branch_source_bytes=$(git cat-file -s HEAD:src/subscribers-cli.ts) &&
test "$base_source_bytes" -eq 1683 &&
source_byte_delta=$((branch_source_bytes - base_source_bytes)) &&
printf 'base_bytes=%s branch_bytes=%s delta_bytes=%s\n' "$base_source_bytes" "$branch_source_bytes" "$source_byte_delta" &&
awk -v delta="$source_byte_delta" 'BEGIN { printf "estimated_image_mb_delta=%.6f\n", delta / 1000000; if (delta > 10000) print "flag for review: source byte delta exceeds 10000" }'
acceptance.expected: After the final implementation commit, command exits 0 and reports BASE source size 1683 bytes (literal from the recorded base), HEAD source size, their difference in bytes, and that difference divided by 1e6 as estimated image_mb delta. The plan estimates +1000 to +3500 bytes, or +0.001 to +0.0035 MB; flag a delta above 10000 bytes for review. HEAD size is an observed measurement, not a test oracle. Read the protected Dockerfile and .dockerignore: Dockerfile copies src into the final image, while test/docs are absent. Scope check proves no other src file, Dockerfile, .dockerignore, dependency or lockfile changed, so this is the whole image content delta. Do not claim image contents or image_mb are unchanged; do not build an image or run the Docker bench (#834). Static import in src/index.ts means parsing a few KB more at service startup, expected within measurement noise; do not claim a measured startup improvement.

The PR body lists every added comment line, or says none if grep exits 1 with no matches. The new test file has no comments except optionally one top line naming the class and expected outcome. Source comments are limited to the accurate existing runSubscribers doc comment, one classifier-constant line naming SQLite primary codes and one escaping-helper doc line naming the escaped set. Preserve unrelated existing comments.

acceptance.command:
ALLOWED='README.md
docs/operation.md
src/subscribers-cli.ts
test/subscribers-cli.corrupt-store.test.ts'
PROTECTED='src/subscriber-store.ts src/index.ts src/failed-cli.ts src/ledger-lock.ts src/ledger.ts src/config.ts src/subscription-settings.ts src/channels/message.ts test/subscribers-cli.test.ts test/index.test.ts test/subscriptions-store.test.ts test/subscriptions-support.ts package.json bun.lock bunfig.toml biome.json tsconfig.json eslint.config.js lefthook.yml Dockerfile .dockerignore .github AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md docs/troubleshooting.md docs/configuration.md'
check_scope() {
  test "$(git diff --name-only "$BASE" HEAD | LC_ALL=C sort)" = "$ALLOWED" &&
  git diff --exit-code "$BASE" HEAD -- $PROTECTED &&
  test -z "$(git diff --name-only --cached)" &&
  test -z "$(git diff --name-only)" &&
  test -z "$(git status --porcelain)" &&
  git diff --check "$BASE" HEAD
}
check_scope
acceptance.expected: Run after the last implementation commit against recorded pre-edit BASE; exit 0. Committed changed paths equal exactly README.md, docs/operation.md, src/subscribers-cli.ts and test/subscribers-cli.corrupt-store.test.ts, sorted as above; no missing or extra path. All explicit protected paths have no BASE-to-HEAD diff. The index and worktree diffs are separately empty, status including untracked files is empty, and committed whitespace check passes. Do not substitute BASE-to-worktree diff or add ignore rules. Preserve this combined checker verbatim in an external fixture harness, parameterizing only BASE, ALLOWED and PROTECTED.

Create this disposable harness with file tools outside the implementation checkout. In a fixture repository, BASE has a.txt and p.txt, and an allowed commit changes only a.txt; set ALLOWED=a.txt and PROTECTED=p.txt and use the identical preceding combined checker. Clean allowed commit: checker exit 0. Reset to it before each independent scenario; checker exits nonzero for (a) protected worktree edit, (b) protected staged edit, (c) protected committed edit with clean status, (d) untracked file, (e) staged protected edit with only its worktree restored to BASE, and (f) committed protected edit with only its worktree restored to BASE. In (e) and (f), git diff --exit-code "$BASE" -- p.txt exits 0 while the combined checker fails. Harness exits 0 only if all seven checker outcomes and both restored-worktree demonstrations hold. Record every actual status in the PR body. Never make deliberate protected edits in the real checkout.

The notify PR body names Closes lorenzh/pulse-meta#<child> with the actual child number, recorded pre-edit BASE and Bun 1.4.0; commands/results for Checks and completion evidence 1-12 and all acceptances above; all three red and green runs with names/reasons/counts (12 fail/3 pass then 15 pass/0 fail); recorded passing BASE/branch controls, including executable schema-version refusal; independent N/S/T/R base-vs-branch bytes and directory listings plus R exact header deltas; ordinary, LF-path and healthy CLI smoke; full check and coverage; ASCII and semantic docs review; all ten CPU samples, medians and delta; committed source byte sizes, byte delta and image_mb estimate; every added comment or none; full committed/index/worktree scope checks and all fixture statuses; and the Security impact checklist. Known limits explicitly include close-throw lock release, first-error-wins and extended SQLITE_CORRUPT_* variants as code-reading-only coverage; same-store-call-order review plus four-fixture evidence; damage found at a checkpoint after a committed delete leaves the deletion and can leave WAL/SHM exactly as on BASE, so exit 2 does not confirm whether the address was deleted; unchanged rollback header rewriting by the store; lock messages still printing paths as given; and image_mb growing by the source byte delta only, estimated without a Docker build. No newline-path exception, universal byte/sidecar guarantee, nothing-deleted promise, Docker-bench claim, service-performance improvement or unexecuted-check claim.
